audit.whatIsWrong: Graves' Q is called 'New Destination' in four places (spikes[0].text, wants.foe[0], early, whys[1]). No such ability exists. His Q is End of the Line; New Destiny is his PASSIVE, and the page has mangled the passive's name and then stapled it to the wrong slot. Separately, Smoke Screen is called a blind twice ('his Smoke Screen (W) blind', 'Smoke Screen (W) to blind your autos') - Smoke Screen reduces sight range and slows, it does not cause attacks to miss. And Collateral Damage, his ultimate, is never named anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: The two errors compound. A reader told Graves has a blind will hold autos and step out of a zone that in fact only takes their vision away, while a reader told his Q is called New Destination cannot look up the actual ability. The interaction the page needed instead is sitting in the real passive: New Destiny fires 4 bullets that CANNOT PASS THROUGH UNITS. A minion between you and Graves eats most of a shotgun volley, which is the actual reason 'never step into shotgun range' works - and it means the wave, not the Q shield, is your armour in this lane. Second missing piece: Quickdraw grants Armour AND Magic Resist, refreshed every time he lands a basic attack, so his resistances against your magic burst are highest exactly when he is attacking - blinking in on a spent Quickdraw is a resistance window, not just a mobility window.
audit.corrected: End of the Line used for the Q with its 1-second/terrain detonation, New Destiny restored as the passive with its unit-blocking bullets, the blind claim replaced with the real sight-range reduction, Collateral Damage named with its 100/80/60s cooldown, and Quickdraw's MR component stated.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (P New Destiny: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units'; Q End of the Line; W: 'reduces sight range'; E: 'Armor and Magic Resist boost'; R Collateral Damage 100/80/60)

audit.why: The chart gives Graves the first six stages and Skill at 2+ items. That matches a 31.43% win rate over 70 games - the largest sample and the worst matchup in this champion's table - and it matches the prose, which concedes the lane outright and plays for the scaling. Both layers agree with each other stage for stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike names Quickdraw as the thing to track and never gives its cooldown, and the ultimate spike is missing entirely because Collateral Damage is never mentioned.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s, but the number is misleading on its own: hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers its cooldown and refreshes the resistance boost, so a Graves who is farming keeps it near-permanently up and the 16s only exists when he is not attacking. Collateral Damage is 100/80/60s. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s, and the 5s-to-2s drop is why the lane only turns at two items.
audit.corrected: Quickdraw's 16s plus the auto-attack refund, Collateral Damage's 100s, and Riftwalk's 5-to-2s spread written into the spikes and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns says 'burst him after the charges are spent' - Quickdraw has no charges in Riot's text; it is a single dash on a cooldown that his own basic attacks shorten.
audit.why: Telling a player to count charges that do not exist means they wait for a state that never arrives. The correct read is that Quickdraw's timer resets off his autos, so the window opens when he stops attacking, not after some number of uses.
audit.corrected: Charges replaced with the real mechanic and the 16s number.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (E: 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill')

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing about how End of the Line actually detonates, though it is the ability the reader is told to fear most.
audit.why: End of the Line detonates after 1 second or the instant it collides with terrain. Against a wall it lands immediately and at full effect; in open ground you have a second of travel to walk out of it. That is a positioning rule the page never gives.
audit.corrected: Added to early: do not take his poke with your back to a wall.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (Q: 'detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain')

edits.before: Graves owns this lane the second he hits 2. His Q (New Destination) splits and re-detonates through the minion wall and his shotgun autos chunk a third of your bar, while your Null Sphere shield only absorbs one instance for 1.5s — you cannot trade the burst back. Last-hit at max range, keep the Q shield ready purely to eat his poke, and never step into shotgun range to throw a Null Sphere he'll just out-DPS. Accept that you concede CS here; the goal is to not die, not to win a single exchange.
edits.after: Graves owns this lane the second he hits 2. End of the Line (Q) detonates after 1s or on terrain, so never take his poke with your back to a wall, and his shotgun chunks a third of your bar. New Destiny fires 4 bullets that cannot pass through units - a minion between you and Graves eats most of a volley, and that wave is your armour here, not the Q shield. Last-hit at max range from behind a caster minion. You concede CS in this lane; the goal is to not die, not to win an exchange.

edits.before: Nether Blade refunding mana off your empowered autos is what keeps you in lane through 4-5 — farm under tower and weather his poke, because a pre-6 all-in still loses to his Quickdraw (E) dash kiting your short-range slow off-cooldown. Level 6 is your exhale: Riftwalk finally lets you blink out of his shotgun range or punish him when his Quickdraw and Smoke Screen (W) are both down. Don't blow Riftwalk to engage — hold it as the escape that stops his roams and ganks from killing you, and let the Q shield blank his return poke.
edits.after: Nether Blade refunding mana off your empowered autos is what keeps you in lane through 4-5 - farm under tower behind the wave, because his bullets stop on the first unit and a pre-6 all-in still loses to Quickdraw (E) kiting your short slow. Level 6 is your exhale: Riftwalk blinks you out of shotgun range, or onto him once Quickdraw is spent - his autos refresh that 16s dash and the Magic Resist it carries, so the window opens when he stops attacking. Hold R as the escape that stops his roams killing you.

edits.before: This is the whole reason you suffered the lane — once you have two items and Riftwalk maxed, the escalating-stack blinks and ability haste let you chain R faster than his Quickdraw can reset, and his bruiser-ADC HP pool has no answer to your stacked AP burst. (His shotgun is physical, so your Void Stone magic reduction does nothing here — your edge is mobility and burst, not durability against him.) He stops being a kiting duelist and becomes a target you blink onto. Just get there: don't int the early lane trying to even a matchup you can't, farm to your spike, and turn the late-game teamfights where his single Quickdraw can't kite a Kassadin who blinks four times.
edits.after: This is the whole reason you suffered the lane - once you have two items and Riftwalk at 2s, the escalating-stack blinks and ability haste let you chain R faster than his Quickdraw can reset, and his bruiser-ADC HP pool has no answer to your stacked AP burst. Your durability never arrives against him - his shotgun is physical, so both Void Stone and the Q shield sit idle and the minion wall does that job instead. He stops being a kiting duelist and becomes a target you blink onto. Just get there: don't int the early lane trying to even a matchup you can't, farm to your spike, and turn the late-game teamfights where one Quickdraw can't kite four blinks.

notes: Wrong ability name, four places: Graves' Q was called 'New Destination'. His Q is End of the Line. 'New Destiny' is his passive, and even that was misspelled. Second error, two places: Smoke Screen was called a blind - it reduces sight range and slows, it does not make attacks miss, so a reader was being told to hold autos for a debuff that never applied. Third: Collateral Damage, his ultimate, was never named in either layer. The interaction that was missing and matters most is inside the real passive - New Destiny fires 4 bullets that cannot pass through units, so a minion between you and Graves absorbs most of a volley. That is the actual mechanism behind the page's 'never step into shotgun range', and it means the wave is Kassadin's armour in this lane while Void Stone and the Q shield (both magic-only) sit idle against a fully physical kit. Also corrected: breakdown.cooldowns told the reader to burst him 'after the charges are spent', but Quickdraw has no charges - it is one dash whose cooldown his own basic attacks shorten, and which carries Magic Resist specifically against your burst. Level chart left alone: Graves six stages plus Skill matches a 31.43% win rate over 70 games and both layers already agree.
